explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Verse 2 says they set out “…to bring up from there the ark of God…” So thirty thousand men are heading out for one errand. I once needed a whole afternoon just to move a cooling rack.

I see why you'd think an altar, but the verse names something else. The trip to Baale of Judah is to bring up the ark of God. Nobody in this passage goes out for an altar. The ark is the whole reason for this walk.
No crown in this trip, friend. David is already king (2 Samuel 5:3), so he isn't heading out to fetch one. Verse 2 says they go to bring up the ark of God from Baale of Judah. That's the errand.

explanations.answer: Celebrating with all kinds of instruments
explanations.explanation: Yes! Verse 5 says David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums and cymbals. That's a full band on the road. My little kitchen timer has never gotten a send-off like that.

explanations.answer: Following behind it in total silence
explanations.explanation: Not a quiet walk at all. Verse 5 says they were celebrating before the LORD with harps, tambourines, cymbals and more. It's hard to be silent when somebody brought cymbals. The whole road was making music.

That's not what the verse says. Verse 3 says Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the new cart, and the oxen show up in verse 6. What David and all Israel are doing in verse 5 is celebrating before the LORD with instruments.

Yes, the ark. Verse 6 says Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled. This is where the story turns, and I think it's a heavy part. Let's take the next verse slowly.
The oxen are the ones who stumbled, but they're not what Uzzah grabbed. Verse 6 says he reached out and took hold of the ark of God. I think this is a heavy moment, so let's read it carefully.

Reins never come up in this passage. Verse 6 says the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God. That's what the text says he grabbed. It's a heavy moment, so let's keep going gently.

explanations.answer: God strikes him down on the spot
explanations.explanation: That's what verse 7 says. The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot. He died there beside the ark of God. This is one of the heavy parts of the story.
That isn't what happens here. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot, and he died there beside the ark of God. The text doesn't mention his hand. It's a sober moment in the story.

explanations.answer: God sends him away from Israel
explanations.explanation: Uzzah isn't sent anywhere. Verse 7 says God struck him down on the spot, and he died there beside the ark of God. This is a heavy part of the passage, and the text doesn't soften it.
Yes, irreverence. Verse 7 says God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence. The text gives us that word, and I'm not going to add any of my own. It's a serious moment.
The text doesn't use that word. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot for his irreverence. Nobody in the story is accused of lying. Stick with the word the verse gives.
Laziness never comes up here. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot for his irreverence. That's the reason the text states. I'll keep to it and not add any other.

True. Verse 8 says David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. Then he named the place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day. Verse 9 adds that David feared the LORD that day.

It's actually true. Verse 8 says David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. Then he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day. The text puts that anger right in the middle of a hard day.

That's not how it goes. Verse 10 says David was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David. Instead he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. He asked the question, and then he hit the brakes.

False is right. Verse 10 says he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. Obed-edom's house is where the ark goes.

explanations.answer: The LORD blesses him and his household
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 11 says the ark stayed in Obed-edom's house for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household. Obed-edom the Gittite is the man who took it in. Three months, and the news is a blessing.

No sickness in this verse. Verse 11 says the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household while the ark stayed there three months. The text only tells us about blessing. I bet that was a relief after the day before.

explanations.answer: Nothing changes for them at all
explanations.explanation: Something does change. Verse 11 says the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household. Verse 12 says David hears a report about it. The news travels all the way to the king.

explanations.answer: Brings the ark up into the City of David
explanations.explanation: That's it. Verse 12 says David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing. After the report, he moves. This time the word is rejoicing.

explanations.answer: Leaves the ark with Obed-edom for good
explanations.explanation: David doesn't leave it there. Verse 12 says he went and had the ark of God brought up from Obed-edom's house into the City of David. The ark leaves Obed-edom's house, and it goes with rejoicing.

explanations.answer: Sends the ark back to Abinadab's house
explanations.explanation: Abinadab's house is where the ark started in this passage (verse 3). It isn't where it goes now. Verse 12 says David had it brought up from Obed-edom's house into the City of David. Next stop is the City of David.
Not this time. Verse 13 says those carrying the ark of the LORD had advanced six paces. The text mentions people carrying it, and it doesn't mention a cart on this trip.

False is right. Verse 13 speaks of those carrying the ark of the LORD, and no cart is mentioned this time. After six paces, David sacrifices an ox and a fattened calf. This trip looks different from the first one.
Yes! Verse 14 says David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD. All his might, friend. If I danced with all my might, my mustache would knock my own hat off.

explanations.answer: Kneels the whole way in silence
explanations.explanation: That's not in the verse. Verse 14 says David danced with all his might before the LORD. Verse 15 adds shouting and the sounding of the ram's horn. Nothing about this walk is silent.

There's nothing quiet about it. Verse 14 says David danced with all his might before the LORD. Then verse 15 says he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sounding of the ram's horn.

That's what verse 16 says. Michal, Saul's daughter, looked down from a window, saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart. The text puts it in her heart, so the contempt is quiet for now. Her words come later.

Not proud. Verse 16 says Michal, Saul's daughter, looked down from a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the LORD. Then it says she despised him in her heart. Her words in verse 20 point the same direction.
Sorry isn't the word the text uses. Verse 16 says Michal, Saul's daughter, saw David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart. That's the feeling the verse names.
Yes, blessed. Verse 18 says that when David finished sacrificing, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts. He wasn't done after the offerings. He sent them off with a blessing.
No warning in this verse. Verse 18 says David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts once the burnt offerings and peace offerings were finished. That's the word the text uses.
No headcount here. Verse 18 says David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts. He's handing out blessings, not running a clipboard.

That's not what she says. Verse 20 says Michal came out to meet David and said, “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” Then she added that he had uncovered himself in the sight of the maidservants, like a vulgar person would do. That isn't sincere praise for honoring the LORD.

False is right. Verse 20 has Michal say, “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” Then she says he uncovered himself in the sight of the maidservants, like a vulgar person would do. She doesn't praise how he honored the LORD.

explanations.answer: Uncovered himself like a vulgar person
explanations.explanation: Yes. Michal says, “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do.” Those are her words from verse 20. They're sharp, and I think they're meant to sting.

explanations.answer: Forgot to bless his own household
explanations.explanation: That's not her complaint. Verse 20 says David came home to bless his own household, and Michal meets him there. What she says is that he uncovered himself in the sight of the maidservants like a vulgar person would do.
A crown never comes up. Verse 20 has Michal say that David uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do. That's the complaint she makes.

Yes, her father. David says the LORD “…chose me over your father and all his house…” (verse 21). Michal is Saul's daughter, so he's speaking straight to her. David says the LORD appointed him ruler over His people Israel.
David doesn't say husband. In verse 21 he says the LORD “…chose me over your father and all his house…” Her father is Saul. The word the verse uses is father.

The maidservants do come up, but in verse 22, and not in this line. In verse 21 David says the LORD “…chose me over your father and all his house…” He's talking about her father. So the missing word is father.

explanations.answer: He'll celebrate and humble himself even more
explanations.explanation: That's David's answer. He says, “I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.” Michal's words didn't slow him down. He says he'll go even further.

explanations.answer: He'll only dance in private from now on
explanations.explanation: David says the opposite. He says, “I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.” Nothing in his answer is about keeping it private. He's not backing down.

explanations.answer: He'll let the priests do the celebrating
explanations.explanation: The priests don't show up in his answer. David says, “I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.” He says I, so he plans to keep celebrating himself.
